a_records.quote: The following counterexample shows that the log-convexity condition is required for Theorem 3.4. Counterexample 3.3. Suppose X_i ∼ Kw-G(x, α_i, γ_i; G) and Y_i ∼ Kw-G(x, α_i, δ_i; H), for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Further, let (α_1, α_2, α_3, α_4, α_5) = (7.1, 2.9, 1.56, 0.03, 0.201), (β_1, β_2, β_3, β_4, β_5) = (8.1, 3.009, 2.6, 1.06, 0.01) and (γ_1, γ_2, γ_3, γ_4, γ_5) = (δ_1, δ_2, δ_3, δ_4, δ_5) = (5.02, 2.05, 1.09, 0.01, 0.001). It is easy to see that (α_1, α_2, α_3, α_4, α_5) ⪰^w (β_1, β_2, β_3, β_4, β_5). Let H(x) = e^{−1/x} and G(x) = 1 − e^{−x}, for x > 0. Also, let (X_1, X_2, X_3) be selected with probability P(N_1 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4) be selected with probability P(N_1 = 4) = p(4) = 2/5 and (X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4, X_5) be selected with probability P(N_1 = 5) = p(5) = 2/5; further, let (Y_1, Y_2, Y_3) be selected with probability P(N_2 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (Y_1, Y_2, Y_3, Y_4) be selected with probability P(N_2 = 4) = p(4) = 3/5 and (Y_1, Y_2, Y_3, Y_4, Y_5) be selected with probability P(N_2 = 5) = p(5) = 1/5, which satisfy the condition N_1 ≤_st N_2. Choose the Gumbel-Hougaard copula with generators ψ_1(x) = e^{1−(1+x)^{1/a}} and ψ_2(x) = e^{1−(1+x)^{1/b}}, x > 0, with a = 4.0002 and b = 4.0001. So, all the conditions of Theorem 3.4 are satisfied except the log-convexity of ψ_1 and ψ_2. Figure 2 displays the difference between F̄_{X_{1:N_1}}(x) and F̄_{Y_{1:N_2}}(x) crosses x axis for some x ≥ 0. Therefore, Theorem 3.4 can not be possible without the log-convexity property of the generators.
